title: edge-affinity-telemetry-arbiter-risk-adjusted-latency-health-fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Implement a telemetry-driven region selection arbiter that chooses preferred POP/region and serving tier for each request using a risk-adjusted composite score. The score combines latency percentiles (p50 and p95), a network-health index (packet loss, error rate, jitter), and a variant-degradation penalty so that the routing layer picks the fastest reliable region and can fall back to compatible model variants when health deteriorates.

Background: Existing heuristics pick region by p50 or by static affinity. We observe tail spikes and short-lived network degradations that lead to higher user p95 and SLO violations. This ticket defines a scoring function, operational knobs, and rollout plan to bias routing toward regions that minimize SLO risk while preserving throughput and cost targets.

Goals:
- Reduce observed client-side p95 across global workloads by 10–20% for latency-sensitive routes within 2 weeks of rollout.
- Route <1% of traffic to a region with composite health below threshold.
- Enable safe model-variant fallback: when a region’s score drops below degrade_threshold, automatically route to a compatible variant in a healthier region or lower-cost tier.

Telemetry signals used: p50(latency_ms), p95(latency_ms), packet_loss_pct, http_error_rate_pct, latency_jitter_ms, regional_capacity_utilization_pct. All inputs use an exponential decay window (alpha=0.2 by default) so recent events weigh more.

Scoring summary (proposal):
- latency_component = 0.4 * normalized(p50) + 0.6 * normalized(p95)  // prioritize tail
- health_component = 1 - clamp( w_loss*packet_loss_pct + w_err*http_error_rate_pct + w_jitter*(jitter_ms / jitter_norm), 0, 1 ) // higher is better
- risk_adjusted_score = latency_component * 0.7 + health_component * 0.3 - variant_degradation_penalty
- variant_degradation_penalty = sigmoid(degrade_factor * (model_quality_regression_score)) scaled to [0,0.4]

Notes: Normalization uses per-model historical baselines to convert ms -> 0..1. jitter_norm is 50ms by default. We keep the formula configurable via Console and infra flags.

Routing behavior:
- Primary selection: pick top-K regions by risk_adjusted_score and then apply capacity, geo-affinity, and cost policies.
- Tier routing: allow explicit tier overrides (low-latency, cost-optimized). Scores are computed per tier/model-variant.
- Fallbacks: when score < degrade_threshold (configurable), a region is marked transiently degraded and requests are routed to next-best region/variant with an automatic exponential backoff probe to detect recovery.

APIs and config:
- New route policy type: "risk_adjusted_region_selector" with knobs: p50_weight, p95_weight, w_loss, w_err, w_jitter, decay_alpha, degrade_threshold, probe_interval, fallback_policy (round_robin|weighted).
- Runtime exposes per-region score and last_updated timestamp for observability.

Compatibility: Works with hosted, dedicated and private deployments. For private deployments there is a local-agent mode that computes scores using internal telemetry only.

Operational considerations:
- Rollout should limit traffic to 5% then 25% then 100% across weeks with canarying across model types.
- Add circuit-breaker to stop using risk_adjusted selector if the scoring service itself shows >1% error rates.

Data retention and privacy: aggregate metrics only; no raw request payloads used in scoring.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Risk-adjusted selector implemented as a pluggable routing policy. 2) Config knobs visible in Console and toggleable per-customer. 3) Automated fallback to compatible model variants when region score < degrade_threshold. 4) End-to-end tests and load tests that show p95 improvement on synthetic tail spike scenarios. 5) Monitoring dashboards: per-region score, routing decisions, failover counts, and a canary health metric. 6) Rollout plan executed using staged traffic ramps.
design_notes: Chose p95-heavy weighting because customer SLOs are tail-sensitive; p50 still keeps average latency in check.
Exponential decay window reduces flapping while keeping responsiveness to sustained degradations.
Variant degradation penalty lets us incorporate model-quality regressions detected by quality ops; keeps routing from pushing traffic to unhealthy model variants even if latency looks good.
Trade-off: heavier health weight reduces cost by avoiding cross-region hops but may increase average latency; knobs exposed for teams to tune by route type.
